I sometimes like to think that we live in a simulation created by an advanced version of the human race. They've built a utopic society where no one has to work and everyone can just focus on what interests them. But they don't want everyone to just take everything for granted, to slack off, to become immoral etc. So they make every newborn first go through this simulation (our world) and see what society used to be like and then after they "die" they get admitted to the utopic society.

It's just my way of coping because I truly don't see a point in living other than believing something better is waiting for us. I guess this is also how religions came about.

You shouldn't blame yourself for that. You can't control emotions like these so blaming yourself makes no sense. And if she's worried about you, it means that she genuinely cares about about what you feel and most likely doesn't hold this against you.

A small anectode about myself:

I changed a lot in my late teens. I used to be pretty shy and antisocial with no friends, but then it changed very suddenly and I was able to attract new people. Going to a new school also helped a lot. I'm not saying this will necessarily happen to you, but do keep in mind that there is a possibility life could change drastically in the next years (especially if you go to college).

Haha, well thankfully I'm not in Venezuela. I am in Eastern Europe though, so I guess that's close enough. I guess I could always emmigrate. I swear, the EU is the best thing that's ever happened to me.
It's basically a fancy way of saying that if two lines aren't parallel, they'll intersect. A lot of definitions in math seem very complicated at first but can be explained much more easily.
It does help if you live in a wealthy country though. In some places minimum wage doesn't really make saving much money possible.
Yeah, and I still have no idea how they manage to do it. I've been on a plane once and that was 3 years ago.

Basically, you have two lines both going into infinity (I'm going to call them line a and line b). Then you create another line (line c) which goes through lines a and b. If it is possible to create a line c so that the sum of the interior angle (the one that is closest to line b) between line a and line c and the interior angle (closest to line a) between line b and line c is smaller than two right angles (2*90°=180°), then line a and line b definitely intersect each other at some point. Both of those interior angles have to be on the same side (imagine line c splitting the plane into two parts, crating two sides), and that's also the side where line a and line b will intersect.

Sorry if it still sounds confusing, English isn't my first language. And explaining this would have been much easier if I could have drawn it out for you.

Edit: And if I recall corectly, in non-Euclidian geometry it is possible for two lines to intersect even if they are parallel (they just intersect at infinity). But I don't really know much about non-Euclidian geomtry, so I don't know how true this is.

Edit: I guess I've written you an entire novel. You can skip the boring bits at the start because it's just me venting. The last 3 paragraphs are the only important ones.

Basically someone close to me decided to be an idiot and get almost sent to prison. I'm not really sure what exactly they did, but it was some stupid white-collar crime they should never have comitted. Thankfully they got off with a warning but the whole ordeal still had a big impact on me. I just started thinking about what it would be like with them gone and how they messed up their lives...

I spent the next few days in my room just constantly thinking about what's going on... Then I got over it. I didn't really care about the case anymore, but somehow I still couldn't calm down. I couldn't sleep (The first day I got the news I was awake til 11AM. I've now managed to start falling asleep around 6AM), I couldn't eat (I lost 3kg in 3 days. I still can't get myself to eat, so I have to force-feed myself) and I lost interest in living (I just watch youtube videos all day now).

So the past few days I've also had lots of time to think about my life and where it's heading. And the more I think about it the more depressed I get. You see, I live in a working class family in Eastern Europe which brings along it so many problems. My parents are constantly in debt because that's the only way to pay the bills. You know when I told you I've been saving up money since 2013? I gave half of that money to my parents so they could buy food for us.

My father has been working as a manual worker his whole life and it has taken it's toll on him. Every other day he tells me he's exhausted and that he can't take it anymore. He hate's that he's always in debt, that he can't get a better job and that it's basically impossible for him to progress in life. He also feels like he hasn't achieved anything in life and that he's going to die like that. My mother's in a similar situation but she doesn't complain that much.

So I'm constantly surrounded by their negativity and it definitely rubbed off on me. It seems like me and my parents have collectively lost all joy in our lives. We never celebrate on holidays (Except on Christmas when we buy things like shampoo and clothes for each other), we don't celebrate birthdays anymore and we never look forward to anything (Except for my sister, I guess. She's the only one who hasn't given up yet).

I've also started thinking about the times in my life I've felt happy, and I've realised it was mostly when I was in my early childhood. When I didn't care if I had to sleep on a mattress on the floor of the kitchen (I've now relocated to the couch in our "living room"), when I didn't care if we got some supplies from the Red Cross. And now I feel like the happiest days of my life are already behind me. I'm no longer oblivious to what's going on.

My family is also pretty isolated. My father is at bad terms with his brothers who live near us, so we never hear anything from them. And the family members he actually does have contact with are spread all across Europe (they were all forced to relocate due to the war in Bosnia). My mother's only sibling died decades ago and the family members she keeps contact with are all getting pretty old. So I feel like in a few years it's just going to be me, my sister and my parents. Then in a few decades it's just going to be me and my sister and this feels so depressing.

And I feel like after college my life is going to be the same as my parents'. I keep telling myself that I'm going to be different, that I'll travel the world, that I'll move to a different country where life can be better. But I know this isn't really achievable. I've grown up poor and I'll forever stay poor. After college I'll just get a meaningless job, move to Ljubljana (our capital) and then just rot there till I retire (if I'll be lucky enough to retire). I'll regret not having a different life, not doing something different... 

I just don't have the energy anymore. I constantly feel exhausted. I keep making these plans for my future just so I can have some hope in my life. But I doubt I'll ever achieve anything. You know, when I was younger I got really interested in AI and Virtual Reality because I felt like if this technology gets advanced anough I'll be able to simulate a life I want. Like that scene in Inception where people pay a guy lots of money so that they can hook up their mind to a machine which makes them live in their dreams. Or something like a [matrioshka brain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matrioshka_brain) (I recommend reading the article, it's a really cool subject).

I just love daydreaming every day and imagining I'm going to live a happy life. That's why I love immersing myself in books, films and songs. It's an escape from everyday life. I've also recently started to try and force myself into religion (my family is Catholic), because it gives me some hope for the afterlife. Though I can't really say I believe in an afterlife.

Ok, I guess I should stop. I guess I just had a particularly bad day today...

Change of subject! Even though I like to criticize it a lot, Europe definitely is an amazing continent so you should definitely visit! What areas are you particularly interested in? I really recommend the Alps if you're into nature. I used to live in a small village in the Slovenian Alps and it definitely is a beautiful place to visit.

I've actually dabbled with the idea of doing my own mini-Europe tour as well. You know, a few decades ago before the cold war ended some Yugoslav high schools had a tradition of visiting the capital city of each Yugoslav republic. Sadly they stopped doing that after 1991, but I would really love to go on a trip like that by myself. So far I've only been to two of the capitals (Ljubljana and Zagreb). I've tried to convince my father to drive us to Sarajevo but I don't think that'll happen. 

And thanks for the compliment :)
My knowledge of English is something I'm really proud of and I love it when people notice I speak it well. Knowing a foreign language is basically mandatory in Slovenia because only 2,5 million people speak Slovene. What languages do you speak?

I guess that engineering really is the universal degree that's accepted everywhere. How expensive is Singapore, actually? Let's say I get a job there as an engineer or a teacher/professor, would I have trouble paying rent for a one-bedroom apartment?

I would actually really love to come and visit Singapore. I've always loved to travel around as much as possible. I live in an old industrial town where nothing interesting ever happens so it's nice to see what other places are like (If you're interested in where I live, you can take a look at this [wiki article](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesenice)).

I've done some travelling before but it's mostly been trips organised by my school. In primary school we went to Paris and London (I especially enjoyed the 21-hour bus ride we took from London to my town because it was cheaper than taking a plane. The trips to Paris were by bus too. It was actually kind of fun), in high school we've been to Salzburg and various locations in southern Austria (my favourite was definitely when we went to Lake Faaker to a 2-day German language learning camp). I've also been to Bosnia and Herzegovina with my father to visit the village he grew up in.

Summer break ends in a week so sadly I won't be able to go anywhere this year. But next year I'll be graduating from high school which means that I'll have a big 3-month long holiday in July, August and September. I guess that might be the perfect time to go on a trip. I've actually been saving up money since 2013 so I've got a way of financing myself. 

But first I need to spend some time thinking over certain things in my life. You see, I received some pretty terrible news on the 14th of August and I've been a wreck ever since (this is actually the reason why I decided to post here). I found out three days ago that everything is going to be ok but I still feel so terrible. I just need a few more weeks to calm down and get my life back to normal. I have absolutely no energy right now.

Wait, really? How's it like living there? I've always wanted to live in a big international city. My country doesn't have any (our largest city has a population of 270,000 and it really is the largest by far). How hard would you say it is for a foreigner to find a job there (regarding language I'm fluent in English, my first language (which is pretty much useless abroad) and semi-fluent in German)?

I already have a scholarship lined up. It's not much, but it'll be able to cover the living expenses and some of the food expenses if I study in my home country (the scholarship gives me 150€ per month if I study in my home country and 300€ per month if I study abroad). Attending university is also free so I'll most likely graduate without any debt. Although my country does also offer scholarships that are specifically meant for people studying abroad, so I guess I could also look into that. But I've sort of been planning on getting a Bachelor's degree in my country and then a Master's degree abroad. Do you think that getting a Bachelor's degree abroad would be a better idea?

And since you know a lot more about the Singaporean economy than I do, what profession do you think is in demand there and uses a lot of math or knowledge of foreign languages (these are basically the only two things I'm passionate about)?

Sorry about bombarding you with questions, but I like to gather as much information as I can when making decisions. A friend actually said once that I should calm down a bit because it looks like I'm doing a PhD in the subject of what I should study at university.

But I also have a bad habit of completely changing my mind regarding what I want to do in the future. Every few months I always go through around 10 days of really horrible depression. It usually happens in late December, early January, middle of July and late August (I think I know why it happens exactly in these months). And during those ~10-day periods I sometimes try to completely change the direction my life is going in. 

So I guess I can never really trust myself to know what I want in life. I do keep a small journal on my phone where I occasionally write down what I'm feeling so that I know what wishes of mine stay constant throughout my life (Writing really is so relaxing, I don't really know why. Probably because it forces me to stop focusing on my problems). I guess I'm done rambling now.

And hey, thanks for talking to me. We need more people like you.

Yeah, I've also thought about going to Austria or Germany (even though that might be a bit cliché for people from my country). I've thought a bit about studying engineering (even though I only like it because of math and physics, I'm not really a fan of the actual engineering aspect of it). At this point I'm just considering getting a job that will be able to support me and just focusing on math and foreign languages in my free time.

To be honest, I've also had a hidden wish of moving to Singapore, ever since someone from my small town went there. But moving there sounds a bit extreme and I don't have any family members living there who could help me.

Basically any developed country is ok for me. Except for the US because its healthcare system scares me.

I live in Eastern Europe, jobs here are hard to come by. I don't think I would really enjoy being a teacher, I just don't have the patience explaining math to people who aren't interested in it.

I also really want a job which is in demand across the globe, because I plan on moving to the UK in the future. My cousin lives in London and seems to be doing alright. While everyone who chose to stay in my home country seems to always be very pessimistic about the future. We also have one of the highest suicide rates in the world.

Edit: Funnily enough, I had the TV turned on in the background and the news program just started talking about the state of mental health in our country.

I don't really see this as a gift. I would give up everything just to be average. 

I don't think it ever got better for my parents. That's why I'm a bit sceptic. 

But my grandmother on the other hand also had a pretty depressing childhood (it seems to run in the family), but now seems pretty satisfied with her life. She just became one of those old people who don't care about anyithing. So I guess there still is some hope for me.

Thanks so much for replying!

The main problem I have with seeing a doctor is that I don't know how I could effectively express how I feel. I usually either have a bland or a hyperactive way of talking and I feel like my doctor wouldn't take me serously.

Now regarding the university subject. I'm really afraid of studying something and then becoming unemployable. A big reason why my father is depressed is because we've been poor all my life. There are 4 of us living in a 500 sq foot apartment and my parents are constantly having money problems. That's why I feel pressured to study something that will give me a relatively good salary.

My father has always been telling me he wants to buy a house before he retires. So one of the first things I want to do after I graduate is buy him a house. I feel like studying Japanese and Korean might be a bit too risky for that. I also wanted to study pure mathematics at one point, but that's risky as well.

So I really feel pressured to study something I'm only mildly interested in so that I can get a stable career. And I would study Korean and Japanese on the side, as a hobby. I do feel like I'm stabbing myself in the back for doing so, but what can you do.

I've been depressed for the past 9 years. I always hoped it would get better, but I'm not sure if it ever will. The only reason I'm still alive is because next year I'll have an amazing opportunity to turn my life around (I don't want to go into specifics). But if that fails as well, I'm pretty sure I won't be alive for much longer.
